q: When two or more electromotive sources (batteries) are connected in series, the resultant emf is the algebraic ____ of the individual emfs.
e: When two or more electromotive sources (batteries) are connected in series, the resultant emf is the algebraic sum of the individual emfs. In series, the same current runs through each part and the voltages add. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop.

q: In series aiding arrangement the currents leaving the batteries are in the ____ direction so that the resultant emf is $E_1+E_2$.
e: In series aiding arrangement the currents leaving the batteries are in the same direction so that the resultant emf is E1+E2. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.

q: A connection of batteries where currents leave in the same direction is called series ____.
e: A connection of batteries where currents leave in the same direction is called series aiding. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals.

q: The total internal resistance of those two batteries in series is $(r_1$____$r_2)$.
e: The total internal resistance of those two batteries in series is (r1+r2). A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals. Resistance opposes current and turns electrical energy into heat.

q: In Figure 10.6 (a) two batteries are connected in series ____.
e: In Figure 10.6 (a) two batteries are connected in series opposing. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals. In series, the same current runs through each part and the voltages add.

q: In series opposing, the emfs of the batteries are in ____.
e: In series opposing, the emfs of the batteries are in opposition. In series, the same current runs through each part and the voltages add. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals.

q: In series opposing, the resultant emf is the ____ between the individual emfs.
e: In series opposing, the resultant emf is the difference between the individual emfs. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop. In series, the same current runs through each part and the voltages add.

q: If $E_1$ is greater than $E_2$, the resultant emf of those two batteries in series opposing is $(E_1$____$E_2)$.
e: If E1 is greater than E2, the resultant emf of those two batteries in series opposing is (E1-E2). Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals.

q: In series opposing, their total internal resistance is still $(r_1$____$r_2)$.
e: In series opposing, their total internal resistance is still (r1+r2). In series, the same current runs through each part and the voltages add. Terminal voltage is emf minus Ir, so it sags when the load current rises.

q: Two batteries having equal emfs and equal internal resistances can be connected in ____.
e: Two batteries having equal emfs and equal internal resistances can be connected in parallel. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals. In parallel, the same voltage sits across each branch and the currents add.

q: In parallel connection, it should be noticed that the same ____ terminals of the batteries are connected together.
e: In parallel connection, it should be noticed that the same polarity terminals of the batteries are connected together. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals. In parallel, the same voltage sits across each branch and the currents add.

q: The resultant emf of the parallel-combination of identical batteries is just the emf $E$ of a ____ battery.
e: The resultant emf of the parallel-combination of identical batteries is just the emf E of a single battery. In parallel, the same voltage sits across each branch and the currents add. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop.

q: Since the internal resistances of identical batteries are in parallel, the resultant internal resistance is ____.

q: In parallel connection of batteries, care must be taken that the terminal of the same ____ should be connected together.
e: In parallel connection of batteries, care must be taken that the terminal of the same polarity should be connected together. In parallel, the same voltage sits across each branch and the currents add. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals.

q: If terminals of opposite polarity are connected together in parallel, batteries may be ____.
e: If terminals of opposite polarity are connected together in parallel, batteries may be damaged. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals. In parallel, the same voltage sits across each branch and the currents add.
